title: Incrementally migrate the Steady backend from Go and Heroku to TypeScript and Supabase
outcome: Steady's existing authenticated users can continue to use the service without unintended behavioural, identity, authorization, or data changes while durable backend responsibilities move from the Go/Heroku/MongoDB implementation to a TypeScript-based backend and Supabase through a reversible, evidence-backed migration, and the unused legacy chat and agent APIs are safely retired after their lack of active callers is verified.
users: The sole authenticated Steady owner-user who records feelings, reviews history and trends, and maintains weekly trackers
Operators and accountable owners responsible for data integrity, access control, cutover, rollback, and production support

in: Characterize and preserve the supported externally observable contracts of the four Auth0-protected browser routes, including methods, paths, authentication requirements, supported request fields, successful response envelopes, JSON field names, and user-ownership behaviour

Normalize accidental browser API quirks by returning an empty array for an empty feeling history, using consistent structured errors and appropriate failure statuses, rejecting malformed or unsupported inputs without writes, and applying standards-compliant CORS behaviour
Omit verified-unused code and compatibility surfaces from the replacement, including the unmatched /api/ping client request and the retired chat and agent APIs
Preserve the existing React application's supported feeling journal, history and trend, weekly tracker, sign-in, sign-out, and session-continuity behaviours during the migration

Retain Auth0 as the authentication provider for this migration and preserve existing Auth0 accounts, subject identifiers, and supported session behaviour without requiring account re-registration or relinking
Implement the replacement backend responsibilities in TypeScript, with the runtime and deployment topology selected only after Design evaluates the allowed compute options

Migrate durable feeling and weekly-tracker data from MongoDB Atlas to Supabase Postgres with explicit schema, constraints, indexes, migration history, reconciliation evidence, and Auth0 subject identifiers preserved as the user-ownership key
Define and enforce least-privilege row ownership for authenticated browser users using an approved combination of verified identity and Supabase authorization controls

Treat feelings and weekly reflections as sensitive private personal data: normal access is through the owner's authenticated Auth0 application session, while authorized operator access is available only through the cloud provider's administrative data controls
Retain all existing migrated feelings and weekly reflections and all records created after migration indefinitely unless a separately approved future policy changes that requirement

Host the Supabase Postgres project in an Australian cloud region and store authenticated-encrypted logical-backup ciphertext only in a private bucket in a separate Supabase project in an Australian cloud region

Use and document the approved Free-plan operator-run logical-backup and restore process, including checksums, encryption, private Australian Storage, retention records, and restore rehearsal, while using and documenting cloud-provider defaults for operator auditing and breach response

Use the repository inventory and accountable-owner confirmation that the retired OpenClaw instance no longer exists and the legacy chat capability, chat ingest, and agent read APIs have no active callers, then omit those APIs and their shared-secret dependencies from the replacement
Create characterization, contract, authorization, data-migration, and rollback evidence sufficient to compare the replacement with the approved current behaviour

Support an incremental cutover in which the existing Go/Heroku implementation remains recoverable until the replacement has passed Review and Release and separate production-change authority has been granted
Document configuration and secret dependencies without storing secret values in source, specifications, logs, tests, commits, or responses
out: Choosing Node, Bun, Supabase Edge Functions, a standalone TypeScript API runtime, frontend hosting, or a final deployment topology during Define
A greenfield redesign of the Steady product, user interface, mood model, weekly tracker, or integration capabilities
New user-facing features, new API capabilities, or new file/object-storage functionality
Adding user-facing data deletion or export features
Paid managed database backups, point-in-time recovery, automated multi-region backup orchestration, or custom operator-audit and breach-response systems beyond the approved Free-plan pilot controls
Reproducing accidental implementation quirks or migrating code that has no verified supported user or integration responsibility
Replacing or retiring Auth0, migrating users to Supabase Auth, or changing current login methods and user accounts
Preserving or redesigning the legacy /api/chat/* and /api/agent/* APIs in the replacement after their retirement was approved
Unapproved changes to access rules, data classification, retention, or deletion policy
Removal of the existing Go/Heroku implementation before Review and Release approval

Production infrastructure creation or modification, production data migration, production environment-variable changes, frontend production API endpoint changes, traffic switching, irreversible database changes, Heroku resource deletion, database replacement, or production deployment without separate explicit authority

acceptance_criteria.given: an authenticated Steady user with existing feeling records and a valid supported Auth0 session
acceptance_criteria.when: the user loads the journal and the client requests GET /api/feelings through the migrated service
acceptance_criteria.then: the request applies the approved authentication and same-user isolation rules and returns that user's complete approved feeling history as a JSON array, including an empty array when no records exist, with the approved field names, value representations, and timestamp semantics and without exposing another user's records

acceptance_criteria.given: an authenticated Steady user submits a feeling using the currently supported mood, date, note, and activity inputs
acceptance_criteria.when: the client sends POST /api/feelings through the migrated service
acceptance_criteria.then: exactly one feeling is durably associated with the verified user identity, the caller cannot assign it to another user through a body or header value, the approved success response is returned, and a subsequent supported history read exposes the saved record

acceptance_criteria.given: an authenticated Steady user selects a week with no existing weekly tracker
acceptance_criteria.when: the client sends GET /api/weekly-tracker with the supported weekOf parameter
acceptance_criteria.then: the migrated service returns the approved successful no-record representation and does not expose another user's tracker

acceptance_criteria.given: an authenticated Steady user creates or edits a weekly tracker using supported mood, checklist, and note fields
acceptance_criteria.when: the client sends POST /api/weekly-tracker and subsequently reads the same user and week
acceptance_criteria.then: the service applies the approved upsert, tracker-version, ownership, timestamp, field-name, and response semantics and returns the saved tracker without creating an unintended duplicate

acceptance_criteria.given: a caller does not present a valid supported end-user credential or presents a user header that conflicts with its verified identity
acceptance_criteria.when: the caller accesses a browser-facing feelings or weekly-tracker route
acceptance_criteria.then: access is denied with the approved status and response behaviour, no protected record is disclosed or changed, and no client-controlled identity overrides the verified identity

acceptance_criteria.given: retirement of GET /api/chat/capabilities, POST /api/chat/feeling, and GET /api/agent/feelings is proposed
acceptance_criteria.when: the repository route/configuration inventory and owner confirmation are reviewed before implementation and again before release
acceptance_criteria.then: the evidence confirms the former OpenClaw integration no longer exists and no active caller depends on the routes; if contrary evidence or a caller appears, retirement stops and the contract returns for explicit scope and access decisions

acceptance_criteria.given: production evidence confirms the legacy chat and agent APIs have no active callers and their retirement remains approved
acceptance_criteria.when: the replacement backend is built and its configuration and route inventory are tested
acceptance_criteria.then: the replacement exposes none of the three retired integration routes, requires none of their shared-secret or allowlist environment variables, and retains no privileged compatibility path that can read or write a caller-selected user's data

acceptance_criteria.given: the React client is running in each supported local and deployed configuration
acceptance_criteria.when: a user signs in, signs out, reloads an existing session, saves a feeling, views history and trends, changes weekly tracker weeks, and saves a weekly tracker
acceptance_criteria.then: the supported user journeys complete using Auth0 without account relinking, re-registration, or an unapproved forced sign-in, URL change, payload change, or loss of the current same-origin/local-development behaviour

acceptance_criteria.given: the current implementation exhibits accidental quirks in empty results, CORS handling, error bodies and statuses, permissive validation, and the unmatched /api/ping client request
acceptance_criteria.when: the replacement contract and React journeys are tested
acceptance_criteria.then: supported inputs and user journeys remain compatible, empty feeling history is an empty array, malformed or unsupported requests fail without writes using consistent structured errors and appropriate failure statuses, disallowed CORS origins cannot invoke protected handlers, and neither the client nor replacement backend contains the unused /api/ping compatibility call or route

acceptance_criteria.given: a non-production export representative of the production MongoDB collections and identity keys
acceptance_criteria.when: the approved migration process is dry-run into the Supabase Postgres schema
acceptance_criteria.then: every source record is accounted for as migrated or as an explicitly classified exception approved by the repository owner/requester, ownership and timestamps are preserved according to the approved mapping, duplicate or malformed data is reported without silent loss, reconciliation can be repeated deterministically without creating duplicate target records, the target project and separate private backup Storage project are verified to reside in Australia, and an authenticated-encrypted logical backup is downloaded, checksum-verified, decrypted, and restored successfully into an empty disposable target

acceptance_criteria.given: two or more users and records created through each approved writer path
acceptance_criteria.when: authorization tests exercise direct data access and every migrated API path using valid, missing, expired, mismatched, and unauthorized credentials
acceptance_criteria.then: each application user can access only their own authorized rows, privileged credentials are never exposed to untrusted clients, retired machine routes cannot bypass user ownership, all cross-user application attempts are denied, and any authorized operator data access occurs only through the cloud provider's administrative controls rather than an application API

acceptance_criteria.given: the replacement has completed its non-production data migration and behavioural verification
acceptance_criteria.when: the reconciliation and contract suites compare source and target behaviour
acceptance_criteria.then: all approved acceptance cases pass, all record-count and field-level reconciliation checks meet their approved thresholds, and every remaining discrepancy is documented with an accountable approval before any production cutover is proposed

acceptance_criteria.given: a pre-production cutover rehearsal has temporarily suspended user writes and switched supported traffic to the replacement
acceptance_criteria.when: the documented rollback trigger is exercised
acceptance_criteria.then: the service returns to the existing recoverable implementation using the documented procedure, every write acknowledged before or during the rehearsal is accounted for before writes resume, and Auth0 user-access boundaries remain intact

acceptance_criteria.given: the replacement is proposed for production release
acceptance_criteria.when: Review and Release assess its evidence
acceptance_criteria.then: the Go/Heroku implementation has not been removed, migration and rollback procedures have named owners, secret and environment dependencies are documented without values, the approved Free-plan logical-backup procedure, private Australian ciphertext storage, retention record, checksum verification, and restore rehearsal are documented and verified without being represented as a managed database backup, the selected cloud-provider operator-audit and breach-response defaults are documented and verified, operational support and monitoring responsibilities are recorded, and no deployment, data migration, environment change, traffic switch, irreversible migration, or resource deletion occurs without separate explicit human authority

constraints: This is an incremental migration, not a greenfield rewrite; externally observable behaviour is preserved unless a named accountable human explicitly approves a difference
The replacement backend implementation language is TypeScript
Auth0 remains the authentication provider for this migration; replacing Auth0 with Supabase Auth is deferred and out of scope
Existing Auth0 subject identifiers remain the canonical user-ownership key through this migration and must be preserved unchanged in migrated records
The legacy chat and agent APIs may be retired, but uncertain usage must be resolved with production evidence and accountable-owner confirmation before their removal
Verified-unused code and accidental implementation quirks are not migration requirements; normalization must retain supported React user journeys and security boundaries
Supabase is the target for Postgres data services and is a candidate for RLS, Storage, and Edge Functions only where approved scope and Design support the responsibility
Define must not choose Node, Bun, Supabase Edge Functions, a standalone API compute model, or the final deployment topology
The existing Go/Heroku implementation remains available until the replacement has passed Review and Release

Zero-downtime cutover and a formal maintenance window are not required because there is one owner-user; a temporary service interruption is acceptable, but every acknowledged write must be accounted for before service resumes

Feelings and weekly reflections are sensitive private personal data; application access is limited to the owning Auth0 identity and authorized operator access is permitted only through cloud-provider administrative data controls
The replacement must not introduce an application-level support, impersonation, service-token, or operator bypass for reading or writing another identity's rows
Feelings and weekly reflections are retained indefinitely; this migration does not add user-facing deletion or export capabilities

The Supabase Postgres project and the separate private Supabase Storage project holding only authenticated-encrypted logical-backup ciphertext must use Australian cloud regions; the exact supported regions are selected during Design

The Free-plan pilot uses an operator-run logical backup and restore procedure rather than owner-accessible managed database backups or PITR; every usable backup requires encryption, manifest and ciphertext checksums, private Australian Storage, a retention record, download verification, and a successful restore rehearsal

The selected cloud providers' managed defaults are sufficient for operator auditing and breach response for this sole-user pilot, subject to their documented Free-plan retention and export limitations

The repository owner/requester is the accountable human who may approve cleanup, transformation, quarantine, or exclusion of malformed, legacy, orphaned, or duplicate source records; no such handling may occur without that explicit approval

The production dependency boundary is limited to the repository-defined Heroku web application, MongoDB Atlas, and Auth0; the former OpenClaw integration no longer exists and there are no active workers, schedulers, relevant add-ons or triggers, external API consumers, or chat/agent callers
Structural validation, readiness validation, and human approval are separate gates; validation never authorizes deployment or destructive operations
Production infrastructure, data, environment, frontend endpoint, traffic, irreversible database, Heroku deletion, database replacement, and deployment actions require explicit human approval
No product behaviour, access rule, identity mapping, data-policy exception, risk acceptance, waiver, or release approval may be inferred
Secret values and private note content must not appear in specifications, logs, commits, tests, reconciliation reports, or responses
The migration must support evidence-based rollback and must not make MongoDB or Heroku removal a prerequisite for proving the replacement
dependencies: Read-only production inventory from MongoDB Atlas covering collection counts, BSON field types, missing or malformed values, duplicate weekly trackers, indexes, validators, database users, backup posture, region, and network dependencies without exposing note content or credentials

Auth0 tenant inventory covering enabled identity providers, issuer and audience, token signing algorithm, Actions or rules, claims, callbacks, logout URLs, refresh-token/session behaviour, user count, and accountable ownership

Repository-defined Heroku web deployment inventory covering config variable names, domains and certificates, deployment pipeline, traffic and availability signals, logging, rollback, and accountable ownership

Accountable-owner confirmation, recorded on 2026-08-12, that the former OpenClaw instance no longer exists and GET /api/chat/capabilities, POST /api/chat/feeling, and GET /api/agent/feelings have no active callers
A verified one-to-one mapping that preserves existing Auth0 subject identifiers from MongoDB documents in target Postgres ownership fields
Documentation and verification of the approved Free-plan encrypted logical-backup and restore procedure and the selected cloud-provider defaults for operator auditing and breach response
Supabase support for suitable Australian regions for the Postgres project and a separate private Storage project containing only encrypted logical-backup ciphertext
Cloud-provider administrative access controls sufficient for authorized operator inspection without creating a privileged application route
A test environment and sanitized or access-controlled representative dataset suitable for repeatable migration, authorization, contract, cutover, and rollback rehearsals
Design-stage evaluation of TypeScript compute, API boundary, Auth0 JWT integration with Supabase authorization, RLS policy model, frontend hosting, data migration, observability, and rollback options
risks: Auth0 subject strings may be represented or interpreted incorrectly in Postgres or Supabase authorization policies, causing orphaned, merged, or cross-user data

Mood notes and weekly reflections contain sensitive private personal information; the Free-plan logical-backup process is operator-run and its recovery point depends on execution cadence, so encryption, private Australian storage, checksum verification, retention evidence, and restore rehearsal must be verified before release
The required Australian residency may constrain Supabase project, Storage-backup, or disaster-recovery options and must be verified before architecture approval
Schema-flexible MongoDB data may contain legacy, malformed, missing, mixed-type, or duplicate records that do not fit a strict Postgres schema
Sparse automated coverage may allow supported route, validation, error, CORS, ordering, polling, or response-contract behaviour to regress while quirks are normalized

If the confirmed-retired OpenClaw integration or another undisclosed caller reappears, omitting chat and agent routes could break it; retaining a hidden compatibility path would preserve broad shared-secret cross-user access
Heroku hostnames are embedded in the Auth0 audience, CORS defaults, client token acquisition, and deployment assumptions, requiring coordinated configuration changes
Parallel MongoDB and Postgres operation may cause lost, duplicated, reordered, or unreconciled writes without an approved source-of-truth and idempotency strategy
The API does not expose stable feeling record IDs, complicating deterministic backfill reconciliation and dual-write idempotency
Production configuration may drift from the confirmed repository-defined dependency boundary and must be checked before release
Removing same-origin SPA/API hosting or changing Auth/session behaviour may create user-visible outages even if individual replacement endpoints work
Normalizing quirks without characterization tests may accidentally change a supported React journey or conceal a caller dependency
A rollback that ignores writes accepted after cutover could restore service while losing or duplicating user data

unresolved_questions.question: What production traffic volume, data volume, latency, availability, monitoring, alerting, and support expectations must the replacement satisfy?
Will frontend hosting remain coupled to the backend and production origin during this migration, or may Design propose a separate hosting boundary while preserving approved URLs and rollback?

approval.reason: Vinicius Delascio explicitly approved the original Define brief on 2026-08-12 and, on 2026-08-24, approved replacing the managed-database-backup requirement with the verified Free-plan control: authenticated-encrypted logical backups, private Storage in a separate Australian Supabase project, checksum and retention evidence, and successful restore rehearsal. This amendment does not waive operator-audit, breach-response, migration-safety, production-authority, or rollback requirements.
